subject: Day 21: three weeks old; 1-month visit prep; tummy time
bodyText:
Today's focus
Day 21. Three weeks old. Week 4 opens: the 1-month milestone window. Avi's head control is improving (brief lifts during tummy time). Arm and leg movements are becoming more symmetric. Recognition of parental voices is starting to show.

Action items
- Schedule the 1-month well visit if not yet booked. Target window day 28-35. AAP Bright Futures periodicity: https://www.aap.org/en/practice-management/bright-futures/bright-futures-tools-and-resources/
- Confirm health insurance enrollment processed — final reminder before day 30. Healthcare.gov reference: https://www.healthcare.gov/glossary/qualifying-life-event/
- Tour 1-3 daycares this week if returning to work in 9-13 weeks. ChildCare.gov directory: https://www.childcare.gov/
- Restock infant Tylenol (acetaminophen) before the 2-month vaccine visit. AAP HealthyChildren on infant fever and medication: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/health-issues/conditions/fever/Pages/default.aspx
- Continue the feeding log.

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Brief head lifts; arm and leg movements smoother and more symmetric. Cradle cap; baby acne mostly resolved. Blocked tear duct possible (continuous tearing one eye, no redness — resolves on its own).
- [low concern] Sustained eye contact during feeds. Early cooing.
- [monitor] Crying more than 3 hours/day on more than 3 days/week could fit the Wessel definition of colic — peaks at 6-8 weeks. AAP HealthyChildren on crying and colic: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/crying-colic/Pages/default.aspx
- [call within 24h] Forceful projectile vomiting + weight loss (pyloric stenosis presents weeks 3-6). Persistent inability to console + arching back during feeds (severe reflux or cow's-milk-protein intolerance). Fewer than six wet diapers per day.
- [call now] Rectal temperature at or above 100.4F (38.0C). Lethargy, refusing all feeds, blue or grey color, breathing faster than 60 per minute at rest, persistent grunting, projectile or bilious-green vomiting. Seizure-like activity. Call 911 for blue lips or unresponsiveness!

Enrichment opportunity
Tummy time accumulating 15-20 minutes today across short bouts. Lay him on your chest at a slight incline if he fatigues quickly on the floor. Tummy time correlates with earlier sitting and rolling. AAP HealthyChildren on tummy time: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Back-to-Sleep-Tummy-to-Play.aspx

Upcoming
- Day 28-35: 1-month well visit window opens; first social smiles begin.
- Day 35-42: peak PURPLE crying curve at about 6 weeks corrected age.
- Day 42: maternal 6-week postpartum visit.
- Day 56-70: 2-month well visit; first round of vaccines (HepB #2, RV #1, DTaP #1, Hib #1, PCV #1, IPV #1).

Further reading
- AAP HealthyChildren on tummy time and back-to-sleep: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Back-to-Sleep-Tummy-to-Play.aspx
- AAP HealthyChildren on crying and colic: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/crying-colic/Pages/default.aspx
- AAP HealthyChildren on fever in infants: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/health-issues/conditions/fever/Pages/default.aspx
- ChildCare.gov directory: https://www.childcare.gov/
